title: MoDaaS evidence record
description: One record in the MoDaaS attested evidence chain (a design note). The language-neutral half of the contract: evidence/evidence_record.py is the Python half, and evidence/tests/test_evidence_schema.py fails if the two disagree on any record. Versioned like a CRD contract -- a change that would reject a record v1 accepted is a new $id, not an edit.

schema_version.description: Pinned. A reader that accepted an unknown version would be guessing at field meanings.

phase.description: Which half of who/what/authorized/result this record carries. Only `decision` is platform-written (a design note point 4).

ts.description: RFC3339 instant. A timezone is REQUIRED: readers sort by `ts` (a design note point 9) and a naive stamp cannot be ordered against another zone's.

correlation_id.description: The run's business correlation id (e.g. `fault-4471`), carried in W3C `baggage`. Required on every phase because it is the key an approver already searches by.

trace_id.description: The W3C traceparent trace id -- the canonical run key (a design note point 1). OPTIONAL because it is never fabricated: a caller that sent no traceparent produces a record without one. The all-zero value is invalid per W3C, so a record carrying it claims a join that cannot exist.

action_id.description: The per-call action id minted by modaas-authz at the first governed touch, or echoed from the caller's `baggage`. Canonical dashed form only.

actor.description: Who the record says performed the step. SELF-ASSERTED on agent-written phases; see `principal` for the attested identity.

attested_by.description: Who wrote this record. `modaas-authz` on a decision (and only there), `agent` for self-reported phases, `approver` for a human attestation. Not a closed set: a community sink or a future attestor is a legitimate writer.

principal.description: The identity the platform established for the caller, e.g. ServiceIdentity::"eaco-policy". Distinct from `actor`: this one was not chosen by the caller.

registry_record_id.description: The governed asset's Registry record id (a design note/a design note point 7), so a decision joins to the approval that admitted the asset.

policy_id.description: The Cedar policy id the decision was evaluated against.

policy_version.description: The policy generation that produced the verdict. Platform-only.

decision.description: The verdict. Platform-only: the one fact an auditor must not take from the party being audited.

matched_policy.description: The clause that fired, or null when Cedar matched none (default-deny). Null is a real answer here and must stay distinguishable from an absent field. Platform-only.

reason.description: Why, in the writer's own vocabulary -- a `reasons.Reason` code on a platform refusal, free text elsewhere.

step.description: Workflow position, NOT time order (a design note point 9). A string because participants number steps `3`, `3a` and `retry-3`.

detail.description: Human-readable context for the timeline rendering.

kind.description: The three governed-asset CRDs, plus Evidence. Evidence is not a CRD and names no governed asset: it is the fronted evidence service itself, and it must be expressible because a read of the audit trail is a governed action that is itself recorded (a design note point 5).

asset.description: The governed asset. `alias` is required whenever the object is present: an asset object naming no asset is not evidence of anything.

attested_by.description: a design note point 4 makes modaas-authz the sole writer of decision records, and the DD's acceptance criteria require a reader to reject one written by anything else.

decisionPhase.description: a design note point 4's field list: the decision record must carry the join keys, the attested principal, the asset and the verdict, or it cannot answer `authorized` for a run.

attested_by.description: modaas-authz writes decision records and nothing else, so this claim on any other phase cannot be true. A reader that trusted the field directly, rather than going through is_platform_attested, would render it as platform evidence.

nonDecisionPhase.description: The platform's fields are refused outside the decision phase rather than ignored: an agent-written record carrying `decision: ALLOW` would launder the fact a design note refuses to take from the agent, and silently dropping it would make the attempt invisible.
